subject: MSA/Order Form: Availability commitments & maintenance carveouts
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@synergia.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft redlines on MSA/Order Form (SLA)

Diego —

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached are Synergia's redlines on the MSA and Order Form focused on availability and support. The high-level asks are: 
- 99.95% monthly uptime for the Dedicated offering (we need this for our compliance audit)
- Service credit cap at 50% of monthly fee per outage month (we've noted Redwood's typical cap but need a higher ceiling)
- P1 response and mitigation target: initial response within 15 minutes, phone escalation within 30 minutes
- Weekly planned maintenance windows cannot exceed 3 hours total per week and must be scheduled in our PST business hours with 14-day notice

Please confirm receipt and tell us who from your legal team you want to coordinate with for the redline loop. We also flagged an item about automated failover — appreciate if Redwood can confirm behavior and metrics used for uptime calculation.

Attachments: Synergia_OrderForm_Redlines_v2.pdf (PDF)

—Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of IT Operations, Synergia AI
oliver.grant@synergia.ai
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@synergia.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 10:07:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft redlines on MSA/Order Form (SLA)

Oliver —

Received, thanks. Looping in Marissa (sales lead) and Hannah (legal) so we can get this routed. Quick responses to the bullets below before legal dives in:
- Availability: We can commit to a 99.95% target for Dedicated in the Order Form, but need to align on what constitutes "availability" (regional vs. global, impact to customer API vs. control plane). Hannah, will propose precise metric language.
- Credits: Redwood typically caps credits at 100% of the monthly service fee over a rolling 3-month window for catastrophic events; we can evaluate a 50% monthly cap but need to confirm for multi-region setups and cached traffic.
- P1 response: Our SRE on-call model supports 15-minute acknowledge for P1s in most contracts; phone escalation within 30 minutes can be included as an operational commitment for Dedicated accounts — need to confirm SLA phrasing with legal.
- Maintenance windows: We can limit planned maintenance to a single weekly window <= 3 hours, but scheduling inside PST business hours and 14-day notice is stricter than our default. We'll propose a compromise (weekday off-peak preference + 7-day notice + blackout options for major customers).

I'll coordinate an annotated diff from our side. Next step: Hannah and Marissa, can you propose a redline counter and an internal approval path? Oliver, can you confirm if Synergia requires measurements against regional endpoints or global ingress? That will change calculation and credits.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@synergia.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2027 08:32:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft redlines on MSA/Order Form (SLA)

Team / Oliver —

I've reviewed Synergia's redlines and drafted a targeted counter that preserves operational guarantees while limiting legal exposure. Key points in the counter (attached as SLA_Redline_Diff_annotated.docx):
- Definition of Availability: "Availability" will be measured as successful responses to customer-originated requests routed to the Dedicated cluster(s) declared on the Order Form. We explicitly exclude downstream third-party failures, customer misconfiguration, and scheduled maintenance (per notice below).
- Uptime Threshold: We accept 99.95% monthly availability for a single Dedicated cluster only if Synergia lists the cluster(s) in the Order Form and agrees to a runbook for failover testing. For multi-region footprints, availability will be defined per region/cluster with pooling rules documented.
- Service Credit Structure: Propose a tiered credit matrix (5%/10%/25%/100%) tied to incremental outage buckets rather than a flat 50% monthly cap. To keep exposure manageable we propose an aggregate cap of 100% of the monthly fee per rolling 3-month period.
- P1 Response: We'll accept "acknowledge within 15 minutes" language for dedicated support with documented escalation ladder; mitigation ETA language must be "use commercially reasonable efforts" with specific time objectives listed as examples (15m ack, 60m mitigation ETA for infrastructure failures). Hard guarantees for mitigation time remain high risk for us.
- Maintenance: We'll accept a max of 3 hours/week planned maintenance if Synergia agrees to a mutually-agreed maintenance calendar and allows Redwood 7-day notice; for any maintenance inside customer business hours a waiver must be signed per quarter.

Oliver: please see the annotated diff for exact clause text. If you can accept the tiered credit matrix and the 3-month aggregate cap, we can move to DocuSign. If Synergia needs absolute hard remediation timelines for mitigation (e.g., guaranteed fix in 2 hours), we will need executive approvals and potentially a premium SLA addendum.

Attachments: SLA_Redline_Diff_annotated.docx (Word)

—Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@synergia.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Malhotra <priya@synergia.ai>, Synergia AI Legal <legal@synergia.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 09:21:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft redlines on MSA/Order Form (SLA)

Hannah / Diego —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing your annotated diff:
1) The measurement definition sounds fine; we need one addition: the SLA should explicitly call out the set of monitored endpoints (we'll provide the list) and the sampling window for uptime calculation (suggest 5-minute sampling).
2) The tiered credit matrix is acceptable in principle, but Synergia needs a clear upper bound per incident month — 50% monthly cap is our preference because our procurement requires an explicit per-month exposure limit. Aggregate caps are harder for our finance team to accept.
3) For P1 mitigation, we understand legal risk with hard remediation guarantees. Can we instead put fixed mitigation SLAs for the first 4 weeks post-cutover (e.g., 60m mitigation ETA) as a short-term ramp guarantee, and revert to "commercially reasonable efforts" after stabilization? That helps us during our audit window.
4) Maintenance: Synergia can accept the 7-day notice and waiver flow. We do need a firm blackout window during our monthly business review week (1st full business week of each month) — please confirm Redwood will avoid planned maintenance then for our declared cluster(s).

If Redwood is open to the 4-week ramp mitigation commitment and a per-month 50% cap (we can accept the 3-month aggregate cap too if you attach a finance-friendly cap note), we should be able to finalize next week.

—Oliver
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@synergia.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft redlines on MSA/Order Form (SLA)

Oliver —

Appreciate the pragmatic asks. Proposed path forward from Redwood: 
- We will add the monitored endpoints list to the Order Form appendix and use a 5-minute sampling window for uptime measurement.
- We'll accept a per-incident monthly cap of 50% for the first 3 months post-signature during the ramp period, after which the standard aggregate cap (100% monthly exposure over a rolling 3-month window) applies. Finance will put a short explanatory note into the attachment for Synergia's procurement.
- Redwood agrees to a 4-week ramp mitigation ETA commitment: first 4 weeks after cutover we will provide a 60-minute mitigation ETA target for P1s. After that period, the mitigation target remains operational guidance rather than a hard contractual remedy.
- We'll include a maintenance blackout clause for the 1st full business week of the month for the declared clusters. Planned maintenance will default to off-peak windows and require 7-day notice; emergency maintenance will follow the emergency notification procedure in the Order Form.

I attached a one-page mutual action plan and a clean Order Form excerpt indicating the appendix where we'll list endpoints. If you confirm, we'll prepare DocuSign and route the redline to finance/legal for final sign-off.

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_Synergia_Redwood.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@synergia.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft redlines on MSA/Order Form (SLA)

Oliver —

Sounds like we have a path to close. I'll start the DocuSign prep and include the endpoint appendix and finance note as discussed. Expect a DocuSign envelope link by end of day tomorrow. 

One ask: please confirm the monitored endpoints list and the primary contact for emergency maintenance (name + phone) so we can populate the Order Form appendix.

If all good, we'll aim to have countersigned paper by next week.

Best,
Diego
